text:
maria: Hey team — customer reported chat responses abruptly stop mid-sentence over SSE. Happening intermittently (~1 in 20 streams). Request ID they provided: req_3a9f2b7c. Model: gpt-open-13b, region: us-west-2. They said it shows final chunk missing and connection stays open. Can we collect a debug bundle and repro steps?

ben: Thanks Maria. Can you paste the exact curl they used and the request headers (UA, proxy)? Also - do we have proxy in front (Fastly/Cloudflare) for that account?

maria: Curl they used (sanitized):

```
curl -v -N \\ \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" \\ \
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\ \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\ \
  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/chat/stream \\ \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-13b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Write a short poem"}]}'
```
Proxy: customer sits behind a corporate proxy + Cloudflare. UA: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT; Chrome). They also tried node-fetch which behaved similarly.

ingrid: For repro bundle we need: full request_id(s) from our logs, edge request id (fastly/cf if any), worker instance logs around the timestamp, and a minimal repro curl that we can run locally. Maria — do you have the exact timestamps?

maria: Root event time from customer: 2026-10-12T21:34:12Z. Our ingest shows corresponding internal request: 2026-10-12T21:34:13Z, request_id=req_3a9f2b7c, edge_id=FASTLY-7a1c. I'll attach the partial server log excerpt below.

support-qa: Paste of worker stdout (trimmed):
```
[2026-10-12T21:34:13Z] INFO Request start req_3a9f2b7c user_id=acct_209
[2026-10-12T21:34:13Z] DEBUG routing -> model gpt-open-13b variant=v1 node=n-12
[2026-10-12T21:34:14Z] INFO streaming chunk req_3a9f2b7c seq=1 size=128
[2026-10-12T21:34:14Z] INFO streaming chunk req_3a9f2b7c seq=2 size=96
[2026-10-12T21:34:14Z] WARN write to client failed req_3a9f2b7c err=broken pipe
[2026-10-12T21:34:14Z] INFO fallback to queue req_3a9f2b7c
```

maria: The customer says the connection stays open on their side; they just stop receiving data (so client buffers).

tony: Could be client-side buffering (Chrome) + small last chunk not flushed. Ask customer to run curl with --no-buffer and -N. Also check if any intermediate layer does response buffering (Cloudflare has origin response buffering settings).

ben: Repro steps to request from customer: 1) Run this curl locally and capture raw bytes via tcpdump or ngrep; 2) Try Node fetch with \"connection: keep-alive\" and \"transfer-encoding: chunked\"; 3) If using Cloudflare, enable 'Disable Response Buffering' temporarily.

ben: Minimal curl we want them to run (exact):
```
curl -v -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <their_token>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --http1.1 https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/chat/stream \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-13b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"count to 50 slowly"}]}' > raw_sse.log
```

ingrid: Also ask them to run ngrep to capture SSE boundaries: `sudo ngrep -d any -W byline host api.redwood-inference.com and port 443` (they might need to run on client side where issue reproduces).

maria: I gave them the curl above. They ran and attached raw_sse.log — last lines show: 
```
data: {"delta":"Hello, this is a"}

[data: {"delta":" test"}
```
Notice missing closing newline and truncation of the JSON in the second event.

support-qa: That suggests the chunk containing the last JSON object wasn't flushed or was cut mid-transfer. We should collect: worker logs (we have a snippet), edge logs (FASTLY-7a1c), and the customer's raw tcpdump/ ngrep / node logs. Also capture server side send buffer sizes and kernel EPIPE traces.

tony: On our side, please run `sudo journalctl -u inference-worker -o cat | sed -n '/req_3a9f2b7c/,/req_3a9f2b7c/p'` and include any SIGPIPE or slow consumer logs. I suspect the write error then retry left a partial flush.

maria: I'll pull the full worker logs and request the customer artifacts. One more repro trick: have them run Chrome with `--disable-features=OutOfBlinkCors`? Not sure if it affects buffering. Also try with `curl --no-buffer` vs `curl` default.

ben: If customer is behind corporate proxy that does TLS termination, they may buffer until a content-length or connection close. SSE relies on streaming flushes. Ask them to test bypassing corporate proxy (hotspot) to confirm.

ops-bot: Debug bundle link: https://internal.redwood/debug-collector/upload?req=req_3a9f2b7c (expires in 72h). Please attach: raw_sse.log, ngrep.pcap, node-fetch logs, browser console network trace, and our edge log export FASTLY-7a1c.

ingrid: Assigning SRE oncall to follow up — @tony please take the edge and kernel traces, @ben take client repro verification and ask customer for proxy bypass results. Maria will coordinate and upload bundles.

maria: Acknowledged — I'll ping the customer for tcpdump and try to repro internally with our proxy staging env. I'll upload the bundle when I have everything.

support-qa: One more think: include exact response headers from our worker (Transfer-Encoding, Connection, Server-Timing) — sometimes a misconfigured content-encoding causes intermediate decompression/buffering.

maria: Good call. I'll collect headers. Closing loop once bundle is up. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
